facts.statement: Struthiosaurus lived during the Late Cretaceous period, specifically the Santonian to Maastrichtian stages, in regions including Austria, Romania, France, and possibly Hungary.
facts.quote: Late Cretaceous period (Santonian-Maastrichtian) of Austria, Romania, France, and possibly Hungary.

facts.statement: Struthiosaurus was a small dinosaur that grew to a length of 2 to 3 meters and weighed between 300 and 400 kilograms.
facts.quote: It was a small dinosaur, measuring 2 - 3 m in length and weighing 300 - 400 kg.

facts.statement: The first fossil of Struthiosaurus was discovered in 1859 by geologist Eduard Suess at a coal mine near Wiener Neustadt, Austria, where he found a dinosaur tooth.
facts.quote: In 1859, geologist Eduard Suess at the Gute Hoffnung coal mine at Muthmannsdorf near Wiener Neustadt in Austria, discovered a dinosaur tooth on a stone pile.

facts.statement: The genus Struthiosaurus was formally named in 1871 by Emanuel Bunzel based on a fragment consisting mainly of the posterior end of the skull and braincase.
facts.quote: In 1871, Bunzel published a treatise describing the fossils and naming several new genera and species. One of them was the genus Struthiosaurus based on a single partial portion of the posterior end of the skull, largely consisting of the braincase.

facts.statement: The name Struthiosaurus means "ostrich lizard," combining the Latin word for ostrich with the Greek word for lizard.
facts.quote: The generic name is derived from Neo-Latin struthio, itself derived from Ancient Greek στρούθειος, stroutheios, "of the ostrich".

facts.statement: Emanuel Bunzel named the dinosaur after an ostrich because the fossilized braincase looked similar to that of a bird.
facts.quote: Bunzel chose the name because of the birdlike morphology of the braincase.

facts.statement: When describing the fossils, Emanuel Bunzel mistakenly attributed some armoured dinosaur bones and osteoderms to other genera like Scelidosaurus and Hylaeosaurus.
facts.quote: Bunzel unknowingly described other material of Struthiosaurus. He recognized that there were bones and osteoderms of armoured dinosaurs among the finds and referred them to a Scelidosaurus sp. and a Hylaeosaurus sp.

facts.statement: Bunzel named a giant lizard Danubiosaurus anceps based on double-headed ribs, a trait he thought was unique to lizards, though these ribs actually belonged to Struthiosaurus.
facts.quote: He named this lizard Danubiosaurus anceps, after the Danube. The specific name anceps means "double-headed" in Latin, highlighting the, for a lizard, exceptional trait of having double-headed ribs.

facts.statement: Three valid species of Struthiosaurus are recognized: S. austriacus from Austria, S. transylvanicus from Romania, and S. languedocensis from France.
facts.quote: Three valid species are recognized by paleontologists: S. austriacus Bunzel, 1871, based on holotype PIWU 2349/6; S. transylvanicus Nopcsa, 1915, based on BMNH R4966, a skull and partial skeleton from Romania; and S. languedocensis Garcia and Pereda-Suberbiola, 2003, based on UM2 OLV-D50 A–G CV, a partial skeleton found in 1998 in France.

facts.statement: In 1978, Walter Coombs classified Struthiosaurus as a member of the Nodosauridae family.
facts.quote: Walter Coombs in 1978 stated it was a nodosaurid.

facts.statement: Cladistic analyses suggest that Struthiosaurus is a basal member of the Ankylosauria clade within the Nodosauridae family.
facts.quote: Cladistic analysis of Struthiosaurus indicates that the taxon is a member of the Nodosauridae and suggested it may be one of the most basal ankylosaurs in the clade Ankylosauria.

facts.statement: A 2005 analysis indicated that Struthiosaurus was one of the more basal nodosaurid taxa, despite having many uncoded anatomical features.
facts.quote: An analysis by Ösi in 2005, describing the taxon Hungarosaurus, found that while being younger in age than other nodosaurids, Struthiosaurus was one of the more basal taxa, although many features could not be coded for it.

facts.statement: Studies published in 2022 suggest that Struthiosaurus had very poor hearing and relied primarily on its armor for defense.
facts.quote: Examinations of the brain of Struthiosaurus published in 2022 suggest it had very poor hearing and relied mostly on its armor for defense against predators.

facts.statement: The small flocculus and short lagena in the brain of Struthiosaurus suggest it was a sluggish and solitary animal.
facts.quote: Its flocculus was very small and its lagena were very short, suggesting it was very sluggish in nature as well as solitary.

facts.statement: Struthiosaurus belongs to the subfamily Struthiosaurinae.
facts.quote: subfamilia: Struthiosaurinae

facts.statement: Struthiosaurus is classified within the family Nodosauridae.
facts.quote: familia: Nodosauridae

facts.statement: Struthiosaurus is part of the superfamily Ankylosauria.
facts.quote: superfamilia: Ankylosauria

facts.statement: Struthiosaurus lived in Europe between 83 and 66 million years ago during the late Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: que vivieron a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente entre 83 y 66 millones de años, desde el Campaniense al Maastrichtiense en lo que es hoy Europa.

facts.statement: Struthiosaurus was a small armored dinosaur measuring about 2 meters long, 0.7 meters high, and weighing 100 kilograms.
facts.quote: Struthiosaurus fue un pequeño dinosaurio acorazado, de solo 2 metros de largo, 0,7 de alto y un peso de 100 kilogramos.

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul estimated the maximum adult length of Struthiosaurus to be up to 3 meters and its mass up to 300 kilograms.
facts.quote: Gregory S. Paul estimó su longitud adulta máxima de hasta 3 metros de largo y su masa de hasta 300 kilogramos.

facts.statement: A 2022 study presented a lower size estimate for Struthiosaurus of 2.7 meters.
facts.quote: El estudio de 2022 presentó una estimación más baja de 2,7 metros.

facts.statement: Struthiosaurus had sharp bony plates covering its hips, neck, and tail.
facts.quote: Sus caderas, cuello y cola se cubrían con afiladas placas óseas.

facts.statement: Struthiosaurus possessed a pair of long spikes on its shoulders and many others along its sides.
facts.quote: Tenía un par de largas púas en los hombros y otras muchas en los lados.

facts.statement: High-resolution CT scans allowed for a digital reconstruction of the Struthiosaurus brain and inner ear shape.
facts.quote: Los datos de la tomografía de alta resolución permitieron una reconstrucción digital de la forma del cerebro y el oído interno.

facts.statement: Brain examinations suggest Struthiosaurus had poor hearing and relied mainly on its armor to defend against predators.
facts.quote: Los exámenes del cerebro de Struthiosaurus sugieren que tenía muy poca audición y dependía principalmente de su armadura para defenderse de los depredadores.

facts.statement: Its small flocculus and short lagenae suggest Struthiosaurus was slow and solitary in nature.
facts.quote: Su flóculo era muy pequeño y su lagena era muy corta, lo que sugiere que era de naturaleza muy lenta y solitaria.

facts.statement: Geologist Eduard Suess discovered a dinosaur tooth in 1859 at the Gute Hoffnung coal mine near Wiener Neustadt, Austria.
facts.quote: En 1859, el geólogo Eduard Suess en la mina de carbón de Gute Hoffnung en Muthmannsdorf cerca de Wiener Neustadt en Austria, descubrió un diente de dinosaurio en una pila de piedra.

facts.statement: Emanuel Bunzel published a treatise in 1871 describing fossils and naming several new genera and species.
facts.quote: En 1871, Bunzel publicó un tratado que describía los fósiles y nombraba varios géneros y especies nuevos.

facts.statement: The genus Struthiosaurus was based on a partial posterior skull portion consisting mainly of the cranial box.
facts.quote: Uno de ellos fue el género Struthiosaurus basado en una sola porción parcial del extremo posterior del cráneo, que consiste en gran parte en la caja craneana.

facts.statement: The generic name Struthiosaurus derives from the Neolatin struthio, from the Ancient Greek stroutheios, meaning "of the ostrich".
facts.quote: El nombre genérico se deriva del neolatín struthio, derivado del griego antiguo στρούθειος, stroutheios, "del avestruz".

facts.statement: Bunzel chose the name because of the bird-like morphology of the cranial box.
facts.quote: Bunzel eligió el nombre debido a la morfología de pájaro de la caja craneana.

facts.statement: Paleontologists recognize three valid species of Struthiosaurus.
facts.quote: Los paleontólogos reconocen tres especies válidas.

facts.statement: Struthiosaurus austriacus was described by Bunzel in 1871 based on the holotype PIWU 2349/6.
facts.quote: S. austriacus descrita por Bunzel en 1871, basado en el holotipo PIWU 2349/6.

facts.statement: Struthiosaurus transylvanicus was described by Nopcsa in 1915 based on BMNH R4966, a partial skull and skeleton from Romania.
facts.quote: S. transylvanicus descrita por Nopcsa en 1915, basado en BMNH R4966, un cráneo y esqueleto parcial de Rumania.

facts.statement: Struthiosaurus languedocensis was described by García and Pereda-Suberbiola in 2003 based on a partial skeleton found in France in 1998.
facts.quote: Y las más nueva S. languedocensis descrita por García y Pereda-Suberbiola en 2003, basado en UM2 OLV-D50 A–G CV, un esqueleto parcial encontrado en 1998 en Francia.

facts.statement: Several invalid taxa have been shown to be junior synonyms of Struthiosaurus austriacus, mostly created when Harry Govier Seeley reviewed the Austrian material in 1881.
facts.quote: Se ha demostrado que varios taxones inválidos son sinónimos menores de Struthiosaurus austriacus, la mayoría de los cuales fueron creados cuando Harry Govier Seeley en 1881 revisó el material austriaco.

facts.statement: The three valid species of Struthiosaurus differ, with S. austriacus being smaller than S. transylvanicus and having less elongated cervical vertebrae.
facts.quote: Las tres especies válidas de Struthiosaurus difieren entre sí en que S. austriacus es más pequeño que S. transylvanicus y posee vértebras cervicales menos alargadas.

facts.statement: Additionally, the contact of the squaro-occipital process is fused in S. transylvanicus but not in S. austriacus.
facts.quote: Además, aunque el contacto del proceso cuadrado-paroccipital está fusionado en S. transylvanicus, no está fusionado en S. austriacus.

facts.statement: The skull of S. languedocensis is unknown, but it differs from S. transylvanicus in having flatter dorsal vertebrae and from S. austriacus in the shape of the ischium.
facts.quote: Se desconoce el cráneo de S. languedocensis, pero el taxón difiere de S. transylvanicus en la forma más plana de las vértebras dorsales y se diferencia de S. austriacus en la forma del isquión.

facts.statement: Bunzel discovered two rib fragments with a confusing construction; they had two heads, but the upper head (tubercle) was short and positioned so it could not touch the vertebra if the axis was in the usual vertical orientation.
facts.quote: Bunzel también descubrió dos fragmentos de costillas que tenían una construcción muy desconcertante. Tenían dos cabezas, pero la cabeza de la costilla superior, el tubérculo, era corto y estaba colocado de tal manera que no podía tocar la vértebra si el eje estaba orientado en la posición vertical habitual.

facts.statement: The specific name anceps means "double-headed" in Latin, highlighting the exceptional trait for a lizard of having bicephalic ribs.
facts.quote: El nombre específico anceps significa "doble cabeza" en latín, destacando el rasgo excepcional, para un lagarto, de tener costillas bicéfalas.

facts.statement: In fact, the ribs belonged to Struthiosaurus.
facts.quote: De hecho, las costillas eran las de Struthiosaurus.

facts.statement: Struthiosaurus is the namesake of the nodosaurid subfamily Struthiosaurinae, whose members are found only in Europe.
facts.quote: El homónimo de la subfamilia de nodosáuridos Struthiosaurinae, cuyos miembros se encuentran solo en Europa.

facts.statement: The discoverer Bunzel sent a drawing and description of the skull fragment to the expert Thomas Huxley in London.
facts.quote: Bunzel envió un dibujo y una descripción al profesor Thomas Huxley en Londres, en ese momento uno de los pocos expertos en dinosaurios.

facts.statement: Thomas Huxley agreed that the skull box resembled a bird's, noting it looked more like a bird than anything he had seen before.
facts.quote: Huxley estuvo de acuerdo en que la caja del cráneo se parecía a la de un pájaro y comentó: "Este fragmento de cráneo se parece más a un pájaro que cualquier cosa [sic] que haya visto hasta ahora".

facts.statement: Nopcsa was the first to understand the fossil represented an armored dinosaur and placed it in Acanthopholididae in 1902.
facts.quote: El primero en entender que representaba un dinosaurio acorazado fue Nopcsa quien en 1902 lo colocó en los Acanthopholididae.

facts.statement: Walter Coombs declared in 1978 that the animal was a Nodosauridae.
facts.quote: Walter Coombs en 1978 declaró que era un Nodosauridae.

facts.statement: Some studies consider the assignment of Struthiosaurus to Nodosauridae provisional until further study and future discoveries are completed.
facts.quote: Algunos trabajos como el de Vickaryous, Maryanska, y Weishampel 2004 consideran la asignación de Struthiosaurus a Nodosauridae ser provisional, hasta que finalicen estudio adicional y descubrimientos futuros.

facts.statement: Struthiosaurus lived from the Campanian to the Maastrichtian stages, between 83.6 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Maastrichtian (83.6 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: Struthiosaurus is classified in the class Ornithischia.
facts.quote: Class: Ornithischia

facts.statement: Struthiosaurus belongs to the family Nodosauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Nodosauridae

facts.statement: The genus Struthiosaurus was named by Bunzel in 1870.
facts.quote: PBDB name: Struthiosaurus (genus), Bunzel 1870

facts.statement: There are 23 recorded fossil occurrences of Struthiosaurus in the Paleobiology Database.
facts.quote: Fossil occurrences recorded: 23
